item.title: PMDA announces web survey on essential-edition medicine and vaccine guides
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-20, the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA) announced a web survey about its essential-edition guides for patients using medicines and people receiving vaccines. These guides, first provided in late April 2026, summarize information particularly important when using medicines or vaccines; the survey concerns readability and other user feedback. The stated survey period is 2026-11-20 through the end of December 2026, provisionally, with multiple-choice responses taking approximately 5–10 minutes via a link at the bottom of each guide. Supporting committee materials describe a two-part approach comprising an essential edition generally limited to one or two A4 pages and a detailed edition, with priority given to preparing and distributing the essential edition. This is a survey announcement, not an announcement of a new legal obligation. item.title: Emergency order suspends specified regenerative medicine at ICVS Tokyo Clinic
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-19, the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare announced an emergency order under Article 22 of the Act on the Safety of Regenerative Medicine (Act No. 85 of 2013) against Medical Corporation ICVS Tokyo Clinic in Chiyoda City, Tokyo. The order required temporary suspension, among other measures, of regenerative medicine using dendritic cells and activated lymphocytes for advanced cancer. An investigation confirmed multiple serious illnesses or other serious events suspected of being related to that treatment; the ministry stated that reports required under Article 18 had not been submitted as of the announcement. The causes remained unidentified, and the ministry stated that it would investigate the circumstances and causes. Original title: 再生医療等の安全性の確保等に関する法律に基づく緊急命令について Government Announcement | Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) | Published 2026-11-19 | First detected 2026-11-20 Monitoring aid only; not legal advice or an official translation. item.title: MHLW announcement: unauthorized access and possible pharmaceutical system data leak
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-18, the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare announced unauthorized access to its pharmaceutical stable supply and distribution verification system. It identified evidence that some stored data had been viewed and attempts made to alter viewed data, with possible leakage of names and contact details of representatives at some companies; the extent of the impact remained under investigation. The maintenance contractor blocked the offending IP addresses and deleted suspicious uploaded files from the reporting system used by pharmaceutical marketing authorization holders to report supply conditions and supply concerns. The ministry announced suspension of that reporting system while investigating the access method; the information website, mainly intended for healthcare professionals, was also suspended, with reopening planned following safety checks. Pharmaceutical supply information continued to be published in Excel files on the ministry's website. Original title: 医薬品安定供給・流通確認システムへの不正アクセスに係る 個人情報の漏えいについて Government Announcement | Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) | Published 2026-11-18 | First detected 2026-11-19 Monitoring aid only; not legal advice or an official translation. item.title: PMDA announces darolutamide and trastuzumab package-insert revisions
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-16, the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA) published consultation-based package-insert revisions for Bayer's Nubeqa tablets 300 mg (darolutamide) and Pfizer's trastuzumab BS intravenous infusion products 60 mg and 150 mg. For darolutamide, Section 7 adds a reference to the electronic package insert for lutetium vipivotide tetraxetan (177Lu) for dosing when used together in PSMA-positive metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer. For Pfizer's trastuzumab products, Section 5 adds a reference to tucatinib's electronic package insert for combination dosing in HER2-positive biliary tract cancer that has progressed after cancer chemotherapy and cannot be curatively resected, limited to cases where standard treatment is difficult. PMDA states that clinical trial results supported the clinical usefulness of these combinations and the appropriateness of the revisions; the trastuzumab comparison also records a terminology change for angioedema under serious adverse reactions. item.title: PMDA announces Rybelsus package-insert revision adding cardiovascular trial results
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-13, the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA) listed a consultation-based package-insert revision for Novo Nordisk Pharma Ltd.'s Rybelsus tablets, 3 mg, 7 mg and 14 mg (semaglutide, recombinant). The supporting document dated 2026-07-15 describes adding results from trial EX9924-4473 as new section 17.1.7 under Clinical Results; it lists the indication as type 2 diabetes. The placebo-controlled, double-blind international Phase III trial enrolled 9,650 patients with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, or both. The excerpt reports superiority over placebo for time to the first major cardiovascular event, with a hazard ratio of 0.86 (95% confidence interval: 0.77–0.96). This is a package-insert revision announcement, not an announcement of a new indication; no implementation deadline is stated in the excerpts.
